 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Brandin Podziemski's performances for the Golden State Warriors have been going under the radar. 
 Steph Curry is usually the one who grabs all the headlines, while rookie Yaxel Lendeborg has made a lot of noise on and off the court as well.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement However, Podziemski, in the three games that he has played, has been doing the dirty work, and he has now admitted to taking a few leaves from Jalen Brunson's book.
 Brandin Podziemski says he studied Jalen Brunson's tricks all summer
 Brunson is one of the NBA's most effective guards, and he played a massive role in helping the New York Knicks win the NBA Championship last season.
 The 30-year-old's ability on the ball, elite footwork, acceleration and deceleration and high-volume midrange and paint scoring are what grab all the attention.
 But what Brunson is also absolutely elite at is shielding defenders with his body, drawing contact and slowing the game down when necessary.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Those are some traits that we have been seeing in Podziemski in his performances for the Warriors recently, especially in the games against the Nuggets and the Timberwolves.
 Speaking on NBCS Bay Area after the win against the Wolves, Podziemski was asked about the above 'tricks' – "drawing fouls, using defenders' momentum against them, coming up under arms" – and if he had picked them up from watching films of other players, like James Harden.
 He agreed that it was from watching film – not of Harden but Brunson.
 Podziemski said: "Yeah, watching film. Watched a lot of Brunson tape this summer, understanding that guys can make jumps in this league, shoot a lot more threes and a lot more free throws. And, you know, back half of last season, that's what I did, and I'm just trying to continue that.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement "I know our team notoriously doesn't get fouled a lot and shoots a lot of free throws. So for me, if I'm able to do that, just reset a possession and, you know, slow the game down a little bit, get the legs back under us, that's what we need."
 Superstars on every team often win games and make headlines, but without players like Brunson and Podziemski, it becomes very difficult for any side to achieve something meaningful.
 Podziemski has picked a great player in Brunson to try and emulate. So far, he has done a decent job on that front.
